title: refreshAllThumbnails: restore active tab even if capture throws mid-loop
description:
background.js refreshAllThumbnails() records the originally-active tab per window, sets isRefreshing, then cycles every capturable tab activating each in turn. The try/finally only resets isRefreshing; the loop that restores the user's original active tab (originalActive) runs AFTER the try block. If chrome.tabs.update / captureTab / sleep throws mid-loop, the function rejects before restoring, leaving the user stranded on whatever tab was active when it failed (and the REFRESH_THUMBNAILS message never resolves, so the Settings button stays on 'Refreshing…').

Fix: move the restore loop into the finally block (alongside isRefreshing = false) so the original active tab is always restored, and ensure the message responder still resolves on failure. Consider wrapping per-tab work so one bad tab doesn't abort the whole sweep.
label: Bug

activity.content:
Implemented failure-safe thumbnail refresh behavior.

- Each tab refresh is isolated so a failed activation/capture does not abort the remaining sweep.
- Original active tabs are restored from `finally`, before `isRefreshing` is cleared.
- The `REFRESH_THUMBNAILS` responder now sends `{ done: false }` when setup or refresh fails, ensuring callers settle.
- Added regression coverage for a mid-loop tab failure, continued capture, and restoration across windows.

Verification: `node --test tests/*.test.mjs` (9 passing); `git diff --check` passed.
